# Chapter 6 — Operational Cadence, Privacy Guardrails, and Compliance Reporting

::: {.callout-note}
## In this chapter
Running risk and AI governance is not the same as running label and retention governance, because the policies in this book watch people. This closing chapter sets the operational cadence for the three reconciliation jobs, formalizes the privacy review that gates every change to a surveillance or AI-posture scope, and defines the compliance reporting that proves — to an auditor and to the workforce — that supervision landed only where organizational position warranted it. It closes Book 07b and hands back to the main series.
:::

## The Operational Cadence for Risk and AI Scope

Define the run cadence and how it differs from the label/DLP cadence — risk and AI scopes change with lifecycle events more than with policy edits, so the cadence is event-driven first and scheduled-sweep second.

## The Privacy Review Gate

Formalize the guardrail the whole book has pointed at: no reconciliation job may expand a surveillance or AI-posture scope without passing a privacy review recorded in the registry. Define what the gate checks (least scope, justification, expiry) and how it is evidenced — this is the structural answer to "why are these people being watched."

## Compliance Reporting: Proving Supervision Landed Only Where Warranted

Describe the reporting deliverable: a per-segment report, indexed by OrgPath, showing who is in each risk/supervision/AI scope, since when, and under which justification — the evidence an auditor and an inspector general need, and the same artifact that lets leadership confirm the org is not over-collecting.

## Boundary, Tooling, and Cross-Reference to Book 07a

Note the GCC-Moderate boundary constraints on IRM, Communication Compliance, and DSPM-for-AI tooling, and cross-reference Book 07a Chapter 7's boundary-caveats treatment so the two supplements share one boundary story.

## Series Hand-Back

Close the supplement: restate that Books 07, 07a, and 07b together cover the full Purview surface — user policy, data plane, and risk/AI — each through the single OrgPath join key, and hand the reader back to Book 08.
